title: Eventual polynomiality of homogeneous dimensions of a finite standard graded module
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $S=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}S_n$ be a standard graded $k$-algebra [def-pc-standard-graded-algebra]. Let $M=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}M_n$ be a finitely generated graded $S$-module: each $M_n$ is a $k$-subspace, the sum is direct, and $S_aM_b\subseteq M_{a+b}$. Then each $M_n$ is finite-dimensional over $k$, and there exist $P\in\mathbf Q[X]$ and $n_0\ge0$ such that $\dim_k M_n=P(n)$ for all integers $n\ge n_0$. The polynomial $P$ is allowed to be zero.

source.place: Tag 00K1, proposition-graded-hilbert-polynomial, specialized to S_0=k, together with the immediately preceding lemma-graded-module-fg and Example example-K0-field identifying the class of a finite-dimensional k-space with its dimension.

proof.text: Choose degree-one algebra generators $x_1,\ldots,x_t$ of $S$ as in [def-pc-standard-graded-algebra]. Replace a finite set of module generators by the finite set of all their homogeneous components, denoted $m_j\in M_{d_j}$: their span contains the original generators and hence is $M$. Projecting an expression in these generators onto degree $n$ shows that $M_n$ is spanned over $k$ by $x_1^{e_1}\cdots x_t^{e_t}m_j$ with $\sum_i e_i=n-d_j$. There are finitely many such exponent tuples, including when $t=0$. Thus every $M_n$ is finite-dimensional. The same argument applies to every finite nonnegatively graded module over every standard graded algebra used below.

source.place: Tag 00K0, lemma-graded-module-fg, proof: homogeneous generators and monomials.

proof.text: Induct on $t$, simultaneously for all standard graded algebras with a chosen degree-one generating list of length at most $t$ and all finite nonnegatively graded modules. By [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components], the finite type $k$-algebra $S$ is Noetherian. For $t=0$, $S=k$ is concentrated in degree zero; step 1 gives $M_n=0$ above the finitely many homogeneous generator degrees. The zero polynomial proves the base case, including $M=0$.

source.place: Tag 00K1, proposition-graded-hilbert-polynomial, outer induction and base case.

proof.text: Let $t>0$, assume the induction assertion for $t-1$, and put $x=x_t$. The ideal $xS$ is homogeneous: its degree-$n$ component is $xS_{n-1}$ for $n\ge1$, and its degree-zero component is zero. Consequently $\overline S=S/xS$ has degree-zero ring $k$ and is generated by the images of $x_1,\ldots,x_{t-1}$ in degree one; it is standard graded. Every graded module killed by $x$ is a graded $\overline S$-module. Finite $S$-generators still generate over $\overline S$, so the outer induction applies to every such finite module.

source.place: Tag 00K1, proposition-graded-hilbert-polynomial, choice of x and passage to S/(x).

proof.text: Using the Noetherianity of $S$ from step 2, apply [lem-trf-graded-power-torsion-polynomial-devissage]. Its hypothesis for every finite module killed by $x$ is step 3 and the outer induction hypothesis. It gives $T=\{m\in M:\exists r\ge1,\ x^rm=0\}$ as a finite graded submodule killed by one common power of $x$, its eventual polynomial $P_T$, and the finite quotient $N=M/T$ with quotient grading and injective $x$-action.

source.place: Tag 00K1, proposition-graded-hilbert-polynomial, nilpotent devissage and largest x-power-torsion submodule.

proof.text: Put $C=N/xN$, with its quotient grading. The images of finite generators of $N$ generate $C$, and $xC=0$, so step 3 supplies its eventual rational dimension polynomial. Step 1 supplies finite-dimensionality of every $N_n$. These verify all hypotheses of [lem-trf-graded-injective-multiplication-polynomial-lift], giving an eventual polynomial $P_N=B+c$ for $\dim_kN_n$.

source.place: Tag 00K1, proposition-graded-hilbert-polynomial, final displayed sequence; Tag 00JZ, lemma-numerical-polynomial.

proof.text: The quotient grading gives $0\to T_n\to M_n\to N_n\to0$: a homogeneous quotient element lifts by taking the degree-$n$ component of any representative. A basis of $T_n$ and lifts of a basis of $N_n$ form a basis of $M_n$. Thus $P=P_T+P_N$ agrees with $\dim_kM_n$ above both thresholds. This closes the induction; step 1 supplies finite-dimensionality in every degree and $P=0$ is allowed.

source.place: Tag 00K1, proposition-graded-hilbert-polynomial, recombination in the exact sequence.

proof_origin.place: Tags 00K0 (homogeneous generators), 00K1 (induction on degree-one generators, nilpotent modules, x-power torsion, injective quotient), and 00JZ (finite-difference integration); dimensions replace K-prime-zero classes over the field.
